Whether an admin who cannot edit is in the console's read-only maintenance window.

top-bar.statement: The console's top bar has the navigation menu, Recently Accessed to the left of the Search menu, the Search menu, the Wand icon (displays ZAgent), the Help icon (context-sensitive help on the Page Help tab), the Tools & Resources tab, the Activation icon (activates configuration changes that impact Internet & SaaS features) and the Account icon (switch between Zscaler clouds and tenants if applicable, view the username and organization information, view or change the password, display language or time zone, and sign out).

quotes: You can also see the pages that you have navigated to most recently by clicking Recently Accessed to the left of the Search menu.
Click the navigation menu to access pages throughout the Zscaler Admin Console.
Click the Tools & Resources tab to access these additional resources:
Use the Search menu to locate pages within the Zscaler Admin Console user interface.
Click the Wand icon to display ZAgent.
Click the Help icon to display context-sensitive help on the Page Help tab.
Click the Activation icon to activate configuration changes that impact Internet & SaaS features.

Click the Account icon to switch between Zscaler clouds and tenants (if applicable), view your username and organization information, view or change your password, display language, or time zone, and sign out.

tools-and-resources.statement: Tools & Resources offers Remote Assistance, Help Portal, Support Portal, Cyber Academy, Terms and Policies and Share Feedback.

quotes: Remote Assistance: Allows you to enable remote assistance so that Zscaler Support can securely and remotely log in to your Zscaler Admin Console.
Help Portal: Opens the Zscaler Help Portal in a new tab.
Support Portal: Opens the Zscaler Support Portal in a new tab.
Cyber Academy: Opens the Zscaler Cyber Academy in a new tab.
Terms and Policies: Displays links where you can access Zscaler legal notices, the privacy policy, and the end user subscription agreement.
Share Feedback: Opens a page with contact information for Zscaler.

navigation-categories.statement: The navigation menu's top-level categories are Analytics, Administration, Internet Access, Private Access, Cyberthreat Protection, Digital Experience, Data Security, Infrastructure, Zero Trust Branch, Zero Trust Cloud (Cloud & Branch Connector features), Zero Trust Browser and Data Explorer (insights, logs such as log streaming, event logs and audit logs, and other log-related settings).

quotes: Analytics - This section includes enhanced dashboards and reports
Administration - This section includes administration configuration settings for various Zscaler services.
Internet Access - This section includes configuration, policy, and deployment settings for various Internet Access features.
Private Access - This section includes configuration, policy, and deployment settings for various Private Access features.
Cyberthreat Protection - This section includes cybersecurity-related insights, policies
Digital Experience - This section includes configuration, policy, and deployment settings for various Digital Experience (ZDX) features.
Data Security - This section includes configuration, policy, and deployment settings for various data security-related features.
Infrastructure - This section includes configurations and networking settings for various Zscaler services.
Zero Trust Branch - This section includes configuration, policy, and deployment settings for various Zero Trust Branch features.
Zero Trust Cloud - This section includes configuration, policy, and deployment settings for various Cloud & Branch Connector features.
Zero Trust Browser - This section includes configuration, policy, and deployment settings for various Zero Trust Browser features.
Data Explorer - This section includes insights, logs (i.e., log streaming, event logs, audit logs, etc.), and other log-related settings for various Zscaler services.

sso-portals.statement: From the console the AI Security admin portal and the Service Portal for Authentication Service can be reached via SSO.

quotes: You can also access, via SSO, the AI Security admin portal and the Service Portal for Authentication Service.

maintenance-read-only.statement: During scheduled maintenance and regular upgrade periods the Zscaler Admin Console is in read-only mode: content can be viewed and navigated, but no parameters can be configured or edited; after the upgrade is complete the console automatically refreshes and enables editing.

quotes: During the scheduled maintenance and regular upgrade periods, the Zscaler Admin Console is in read-only mode. You can view content and navigate through the Zscaler Admin Console to view various details.
You cannot configure or edit any parameters when the Zscaler Admin Console is in read-only mode. After the upgrade is complete, the Zscaler Admin Console automatically refreshes and enables editing.

home-page.statement: The home page appears when an admin logs in to the Zscaler Admin Console and its cards can be added, deleted, rearranged and resized; Customize in the lower-right corner begins editing, and the resize icon toggles a card between half and full size.

quotes: The home page appears when you log in to the Zscaler Admin Console. You can add, delete, rearrange, and resize the cards on the page to best suit your working requirements and preferences.
click the resize icon to toggle between a half- and a full-size card
Click Customize in the lower-right corner to begin editing the page

home-cards.statement: The six analytics cards are Networking, Private Applications, Digital Experience, Cybersecurity, Devices, and Appliances, each drawn from the matching dashboard, and Go to Full View in the lower-right corner of an analytics card displays the complete dashboard; the other cards are Recently Viewed (the pages navigated to most recently), News (articles curated by Zscaler on internet security topics), Learn About Products (videos) and Resources (technical documentation, product tours and a feedback form).

quotes: Networking: Shows the network traffic information graphs from the Networking dashboard.
Private Applications: Shows information about applications in your organization from the Applications dashboard.
Digital Experience: Shows the overall digital experience graph from the Digital Experience dashboard.
Cybersecurity: Shows the cybersecurity transactions graph from the Cybersecurity dashboard.
Devices: Shows the user devices graph from the Devices dashboard.
Appliances: Shows the deployment and active status charts from the Appliances dashboard.
To display the complete dashboard for any analytics card, click Go to Full View in the lower-right corner of the card.
The Recently Viewed card contains a list of the pages that you navigated to most recently.
The News card contains a list of news articles, curated by Zscaler, that are internet security-related topics of interest.
The Learn About Products card contains videos about Zscaler products and services.
The Resources card contains links to Zscaler technical documentation, product tours, and a form where you can provide feedback.

search.statement: Search results include Zscaler Admin Console pages (except items in the Help menu) and do not include field names, toggle names or tooltips; Ctrl+K sets the cursor focus on the Search menu, search provides auto-complete suggestions and keeps a history of recent searches, and Recently Accessed lists the pages recently selected from search results or navigated to.

quotes: Search results include Zscaler Admin Console pages (except for items in the Help menu) and do not include:
Field names
Toggle names
Tooltips
press Ctrl+K to set your cursor's focus on the menu
Search provides auto-complete suggestions as you type.
Search keeps a history of your recent searches.
You can see the pages that you have selected from search results or navigated to most recently by clicking Recently Accessed to the left of the Search menu.

account-menu.statement: The account menu shows the Login ID (the ID used to log in to the Zscaler Admin Console), the Organization ID (the unique identifier of the organization), a Private Access Microtenant choice when the organization has multiple Private Access (ZPA) Microtenants, and the Internet & SaaS and Private Access clouds provisioned for the organization; when an admin changes clouds, the admin sees only the entitlements granted on that cloud.

quotes: Login ID: The ID you use to log in to the Zscaler Admin Console.
Organization ID: The unique identifier of your organization.
Private Access Microtenant: If your organization has multiple Private Access (ZPA) Microtenants, you can select the one you want from the drop-down menu, or use the default.
Internet & SaaS Cloud: Select the Internet & SaaS cloud that has been provisioned for your organization.
Private Access Cloud: Select the Private Access cloud that has been provisioned for your organization.

evidence.after: Private Access Cloud: Select the Private Access cloud that has been provisioned
quotes: When you change clouds, you only see the entitlements granted to you on that cloud.

default-clouds.statement: Default Internet & SaaS Cloud and Default Private Access Cloud choose the clouds an admin logs in to by default; the page says the Private Access drop-down menu is displayed if there is only one cloud that has been provisioned for the organization.

quotes: Default Internet & SaaS Cloud: Select the Internet & SaaS cloud you want to log in to by default.

Default Private Access Cloud: Select the Private Access cloud you want to log in to by default. The drop-down menu is displayed if there is only one cloud that has been provisioned for your organization.

languages.statement: In some locations the user interface language can be changed to English (US), Chinese (Traditional), French, German, Japanese or Spanish.

quotes: Language: In some locations, you can change the user interface to display one of the following languages:

evidence.after: Language: In some locations, you can change the user interface to display one of the following languages:
quotes: English (US)
Chinese (Traditional)
- French
- German
- Japanese
- Spanish

time-zone.statement: The Zscaler service saves transactions in UTC and the account time zone is used only for exporting logs to CSV files; it does not affect the generated logs in the console, because the system time zone determines their time stamp.

quotes: When the Zscaler service saves transactions, it uses UTC (Coordinated Universal Time). The time zone is used only for exporting logs to CSV files.
It does not affect the generated logs in the Zscaler Admin Console because the system time zone determines the time stamp of the generated logs.

password.statement: The console password must contain at least 8 characters and include 1 number, 1 uppercase character and 1 special character, and only ASCII characters are allowed; the Zscaler service applies the strongest restrictions and complexity.

quotes: The Zscaler service applies the strongest restrictions and complexity.
The password must contain at least 8 characters and include 1 number, 1 uppercase character, and 1 special character. Only ASCII characters are allowed.

theme-and-navigation.statement: Account settings choose a Light, Dark or System theme for the Admin Console (System applies the device's system display theme preference).

quotes: Theme: Choose the display setting to apply to the Zscaler Admin Console for your account:
Light Theme: The light mode display theme is always used.
Dark Theme: The dark mode display theme is always used.
System Theme: Applies your device's system display theme preference.

table-settings-storage.statement: Every time an admin changes a table's settings they are stored in the browser's local storage so that the changes are preserved at the next logon; clearing the cache or using a different browser loses the settings, and not all settings are available for all tables.

quotes: Every time you make a change, the settings are stored in your browser's local storage so that your changes are preserved the next time you log on. If you clear your cache or use a different browser, your settings are lost.
Not all settings are available for all tables.

table-behaviors.statement: Table search shows the applicable rows even if the term is in a hidden column; resetting columns to default settings does not affect sort order; clipped data can be viewed in a tooltip; for some tables at least one column must be visible at all times, and the page's example is that for Insight log tables Deselect All columns renders the table empty; and Save Applied Filter saves a filter, with an Information icon next to the filter name indicating unsaved changes.

quotes: The search results display the applicable rows even if the term is in a hidden column.
Resetting columns to default settings does not affect sort order.
You can view the clipped data in the tooltip.
For some tables, you must have at least one column visible at all times. For example, for Insight log tables, you can Deselect All columns and render the table empty.
Click Save Applied Filter.
An Information icon next to the filter name indicates unsaved changes.

supported-browsers.statement: On Windows 10 and later the console supports the two most recent versions of Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox and Microsoft Edge; on macOS 10 and later it supports the two most recent versions of Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox. The page says older versions of these browsers should be compatible but are no longer actively tested, and other browsers should be compatible but are not actively tested.

quotes: The Zscaler Admin Console supports the following browsers on Windows 10 and later:
Microsoft Edge (two most recent versions)
The Zscaler Admin Console supports the following browsers on macOS 10 and later:
Google Chrome (two most recent versions)
Mozilla Firefox (two most recent versions)
Older versions of these browsers should be compatible, but are no longer actively tested.
Other browsers should be compatible, but are not actively tested.
Google Chrome (two most recent versions)
Mozilla Firefox (two most recent versions)

remote-assistance.statement: Remote Assistance allows Zscaler Support to securely and remotely log in to the Zscaler Admin Console with either view-only or full admin privileges, without creating new admin accounts or sharing passwords; only admin users with Remote Assistance Management enabled for their role can make changes in the Remote Assistance window, opened by clicking the Help icon, selecting the Tools & Resources tab and clicking Remote Assistance.

quotes: With Remote Assistance, you can allow Zscaler Support to securely and remotely log in to your Zscaler Admin Console. This can be done with either view-only or full admin privileges.
You do not need to create new admin accounts or share passwords to enable access for either option.
Only admin users with Remote Assistance Management enabled for their role can make changes in the Remote Assistance window.
Click the Help icon and then select the Tools & Resources tab.
Click Remote Assistance. In the Remote Assistance window:

remote-assistance-options.statement: Either or both options can be chosen: View-Only lets Zscaler Support view the screen without making changes, with an Access Ends On date within 90 days after which view-only access automatically expires; Full Access (Read/Write) lets Zscaler Support read data and make changes, with an Access Ends In time after which full access automatically expires.

quotes: You can choose one or both of the following options:
View-Only: Select this option to allow Zscaler Support to be able to view your screen, but not have access to make changes in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Access Ends On: Enter a date within 90 days. After this date, view-only access by Zscaler Support automatically expires.
Full Access (Read/Write): Select this option to allow Zscaler Support to read data and make changes in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Access Ends In: Select a time, after which full access by Zscaler Support automatically expires.

remote-assistance-obfuscate.statement: Obfuscate Data conceals user names, data and device information (such as device name, hostname and owner) from Zscaler Support, and after Remote Assistance is enabled the console displays a message that Remote Assistance is enabled until the access time expires or Remote Assistance is disabled.

quotes: Obfuscate Data: Enable to conceal user names, data, and device information (e.g., device name, hostname, and owner) from Zscaler Support.
After Remote Assistance is enabled, the Zscaler Admin Console displays a message alerting users that Remote Assistance is enabled until the access time expires or Remote Assistance is disabled.

remote-assistance-duration.summary: The Experience Center page bounds view-only Remote Assistance access to a date within 90 days; the Cloud & Branch Connector page, for the same Help > Tools & Resources > Remote Assistance path, recommends a length of at least one year for view-only access.

quotes: Access Ends On: Enter a date within 90 days. After this date, view-only access by Zscaler Support automatically expires.

positions.says: View-only access ends on a date within 90 days.

quotes: Go to Help > Tools & Resources > Remote Assistance.
Zscaler recommends that you select a length of at least one year when choosing view-only access and at least two days when choosing full access.

positions.says: Zscaler recommends at least one year for view-only access (existing claim cloud-connector.support-access:durations).

remote-assistance-duration.impact: A recommendation of one year or more for view-only access is outside the 90 days the Experience Center page allows; the pages do not say whether the settings are the same or whether the limit differs by page.

home-card-ranges.title: The time ranges the home page cards show
home-card-ranges.detail: The Viewing the Experience Center Home Page article does not state the time range of the data on its analytics cards.

search-exclusions.title: The search exclusion list's fourth item
search-exclusions.detail: The search page's list of what results do not include has a fourth item, Tabs, on a line too short to quote; the quoted items are field names, toggle names and tooltips.

default-private-access-cloud.title: When the Default Private Access Cloud drop-down is displayed
default-private-access-cloud.detail: The page says the drop-down menu is displayed if there is only one cloud provisioned, which reads inverted; nothing confirms either reading.

browsers-unlisted.title: Whether Safari and Linux browsers are supported
browsers-unlisted.detail: The supported-browsers page lists Chrome, Firefox and Edge on Windows 10 and later and Chrome and Firefox on macOS 10 and later; Safari and Linux are not listed on it.

remote-assistance-api.title: Whether the ZIA legacy remote assistance API sets the same console setting
remote-assistance-api.detail: The ZIA legacy API /remoteAssistance (legacy-api-remote-assistance-support.json: viewOnlyUntil, fullAccessUntil, usernameObfuscated, deviceInfoObfuscate) has fields that look like the console's options; whether it sets the same setting is not checked here.

full-access-longest.title: The longest Full Access time for Remote Assistance
full-access-longest.detail: The Enabling Remote Assistance page says Access Ends In is a time after which full access expires, and does not give the longest time.
